title: Basic variables
description:
## Vars
If you come from other languages, you probably think of variables as mutible little bundles of data. Not in haskell. Basically, variables are immutible period in haskell. Technically its possible, but it involves references. _Yeah, that manual memory managment thing_. To create a var in haskell, you use:
```haskell
var <VarName> = <value>
```
. Pretty simple!
## String concatenation.
You concatenate strings in haskell with the `++` operator.
```haskell
putStrLn ("Hello, " ++ "World!")
```
Notice the () around the ++ in the previous line: that is because functions in haskells precedency is BEFORE the ++, and () basically says evaluate what's inside these () first. Without the (), it would try and print the first message--"Hello, ",--then try and conacatenate nothing with a string, causing an error.
